# `Time.Timestamp`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Time.Timestamp — an opaque instant in time (Layer 3 Ipe source).

A `Timestamp` represents a single point in time as milliseconds since the
Unix epoch.  The ONLY way to build one is `fromUnixMillis` (any `Int` is a
valid instant); the raw millisecond value is recovered for runtime kernels
via `toUnixMillis`.

Because `Timestamp` and `Ipe.Duration` are distinct types, adding two
instants together or subtracting a format-width from a clock read are
type errors — only the operations that make semantic sense compile:
`add` shifts an instant by a span; `diff` measures the span between two
instants.

## `Timestamp`

An opaque instant carried as whole milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
The constructor is NOT exported, so no raw `Int` can accidentally stand in
for a `Timestamp`.

## `fromUnixMillis`

```ipe
fromUnixMillis : Int -> Timestamp
```

`fromUnixMillis ms` — the only `Timestamp` constructor.  Total: every `Int`
represents a valid instant (negative values are instants before the epoch).

## `toUnixMillis`

```ipe
toUnixMillis : Timestamp -> Int
```

`toUnixMillis t` — recover the raw millisecond value for runtime kernels.

## `add`

```ipe
add : Duration -> Timestamp -> Timestamp
```

`add span t` — shift instant `t` forward by `span`.  A negative span
(which `Duration` prevents by clamping to zero) results in `t` unchanged.

## `diff`

```ipe
diff : Timestamp -> Timestamp -> Duration
```

`diff a b` — the `Duration` from instant `b` to instant `a`.  The result
is clamped to zero when `b` is after `a` (preserving `Duration` non-negativity).
